sources.label: This site, build 1.60.1.70009's engine fork (sim/core target auto-attack, attack table and TMI)
Blizzard, Deep Dive panel recap (the Phase 1 raid is the level 60 content the beta does not yet reach)

cmangos classic-db (ClassicDB_1_12_1_z2815), creature_template_classlevelstats: BaseMeleeAttackPower for creature class 1 (warrior) by level; level 63 is 268, the attack power the db gives Ragnaros, Nefarian and the other level 63 warrior-class raid bosses

Blizzard Classic forums, "Boss Attacks and You" (2020-03-03): a creature's swing is weapon damage x (1 + 0.15873% x attack power), a level 63 boss has about 270 attack power, so removing all of it takes about 30% off its melee
vmangos core, Creature::UpdateDamagePhysical: weapon damage x (0.7 + 0.3 x attack power / database attack power), the same 30% share

notes: The one statement of the fight every tank spec is simmed against: what a tank's BiS rows, stat weights and headline figures (effective health, damage taken per second, chance of death, threat per second) are measured on. Nothing public states a Forever raid boss's melee numbers (the beta stops at level 30 and no Phase 1 boss has been datamined), so this is a stand-in, built so every figure is a RELATIVE comparison between sets and none is a prediction of a named boss; the reasons below say what each number stands for and what would change it. The boss is the target the character already fights (level 63 at 60: api.DefaultTargetLevel), tanked by the character, hitting with one melee swing; crushing blows and critical hits come from the engine's own attack table for the three-level gap, not from a number here. The tank carries the Phase 1 raid buffs and tank consumables of data/curated/presets.json's raid preset when ranked raid-ready, and the class kit alone when ranked bare. Bands below 60 fight the same boss with its damage scaled by the heal profile's dungeon table (data/curated/heal-profile.json bands): the band's tank hit over the reference band's, the hit its dungeons' last bosses and hardest trash pulls land on the group's tank, sourced from cmangos classic-db and the beta logs' tank share. The healers keep the stand-in's ratio of healing to damage, (band level over 60) to the power level_scaling.healing_exponent less level_scaling.exponent, because a low-level tank's armor and avoidance take less of each swing. A level between two bands fights the band at or below it, the heal profile's band rule, because it wears that band's gear; a level below 20 scales down from band 20 by level_scaling.exponent. Sim-accuracy round 30 moved the bands onto the table: the old (band level over 60) squared made the boss 1.4 to 2 times the table from 20 to 50.

exponent.reason: Below band 20, the lowest row of the heal profile's dungeon table, damage scales down from band 20 as (character level over 20) to this power, because a tank's health grows faster than its level. Bands 20 to 50 take the table instead (notes); the old stand-in, (band level over 60) to this power at every band, hit 1.4 to 2 times harder than the table (sim-accuracy round 30).

healing_exponent.reason: Healing keeps the stand-in's ratio to the damage: the damage scale times (fight level over 60) to the power healing_exponent less exponent, so a lower level is healed a little more for the damage it takes, because a low-level tank's armor and avoidance take less of each swing and its healers' output is spell ranks and mana the damage does not shrink with. Sim-accuracy round 30 measured that ratio as close to a dungeon healer's (round 29 walks-heal T2) and kept it; healing the bands by the table ratio alone left a bare tank at 20 to 39 dying in every fight.

swing_speed_sec.reason: One melee swing every 2.0 seconds, the cadence of most Classic raid melee bosses. A faster boss favours block value and avoidance streaks less than a slower, harder-hitting one; 2.0 s sits between.

min_base_damage.reason: The least a swing rolls before armor at the reference level, with the boss's full attack power (attack_power_by_level) in it; the weapon roll under it is this divided by (1 + attack power x the engine's 0.15873%), so attack power changes the shape of nothing until something lowers it. The engine rolls the minimum up to (1 + damage spread) times it, so the mean unmitigated swing is about 2,900 at level 60. Chosen so a raid-ready level 60 tank takes a few hundred damage per second and is rarely killed, while a bare one is killed in a real share of fights: the range in which armor, avoidance and health all move the result.

attack_power_by_level.reason: The boss's melee attack power at its own level (the target level, three above the character's): a Classic warrior-class creature's, 268 at level 63, from cmangos classic-db's creature_template_classlevelstats (Blizzard's Classic testing puts a level 63 boss at about 270). A creature's swing scales with it as a share (weapon damage x (1 + 0.15873% x attack power)), so it is about 30% of a level 63 boss's swing and 11% of a level 23 one's. It is here so Demoralizing Shout and Demoralizing Roar take off what they take in the game: at 60, 204 attack power is about 23% of the boss's melee. It does not change the mean swing (min_base_damage includes it); only attack power reductions do.

damage_spread.reason: The engine's own enemy swing rule (sim/core/attack.go EnemyWeaponDamage): a swing rolls between the minimum and 133% of it, so the spread is 0.33. Kept as the engine states it.

parry_haste.reason: A parried swing advances the boss's next swing, as in Classic. It makes parry worth less than the avoided damage alone suggests, which the weights should show.

dual_wield.reason: A single melee swing. Raid bosses that dual wield are rare and would only double the table the tank rolls against.

hps.reason: Healing per second the tank receives at level 60, the output of the healers the raid assigns to the main tank. The healers are assumed, not simulated: they heal in a steady cadence regardless of the tank's health, so chance of death measures how often the tank's health runs out between heals and total damage taken cannot be undone by a fast heal. Set so that a poorly mitigated set dies in a real share of fights, because the healers cannot catch up with its spikes, and a well mitigated one rarely does.

cadence_sec.reason: The healers' median time between heals on the tank, the engine's default when unset.

cadence_variation_sec.reason: How far each heal lands from the median cadence. Real healing arrives unevenly; a variation of a quarter of the cadence keeps the chance-of-death figure from depending on one lucky run of heals.

burst_window_sec.reason: The TMI window. The engine's published TMI is the log-sum of damage in sliding windows of this length as a share of the tank's health, the standard 6 seconds, so spiky incoming damage is penalised the way a healer's reaction time would punish it.
